flagged.evidence: The statement assumes only that "f(z)=w has exactly one solution a inside Γ, and that solution is simple," then concludes "a=(1/2π i)∫_Γ ζ f'(ζ)/(f(ζ)-w)dζ." But `thm-weighted-argument-principle` proves `(1/2π i)∫_Γ g(z)f'(z)/f(z)dz = Σ_a n(Γ,a) ord_a(f) g(a) - Σ_b n(Γ,b) ord_b^{pole}(f) g(b)`, so a unique simple zero contributes `n(Γ,a)a`, not just `a`. Counterexample: take Ω=C, f(z)=z, w=1, and Γ(t)=1+(1/2)e^{4πit}. Then `f(z)=w` has the unique simple solution `a=1` inside Γ, but `n(Γ,1)=2`, so the integral equals `2`, not `1`.

Step 2.1 says: "the standard regularization theorem used in the source sections gives a decreasing sequence (u_ν) of smooth plurisubharmonic functions on neighborhoods of F(K) ..." None of the opened dependencies states that approximation theorem. `thm-decreasing-limits-of-plurisubharmonic-functions` only says what happens to a decreasing sequence once it is given; `thm-c-two-levi-criterion-for-plurisubharmonicity` and `thm-chain-rule-for-holomorphic-maps-in-several-variables` only cover the smooth case. So the general case is imported from the source notes rather than proved from current disk.

Step 1.2 concludes: "Since restriction commutes with taking pointwise suprema and upper-semicontinuous regularization, the line restriction of V is subharmonic." The opened dependencies do not license that identification. `def-upper-semicontinuous-regularization` defines `v^*(z)=limsup_{w→z} v(w)` on an open set, while the line component used here is not open in Ω; approaching `z` inside Ω allows off-line directions, so `(v^*)|_L` is not justified as the same object as the upper-semicontinuous regularization of `v|_L`. Without that extra claim, [L3] proves subharmonicity only for the restricted regularization, not for the actual restriction of `V`.

Step 1.2 begins, "The standard Levi-form decomposition used in the harvested Boas proof yields a constant C>0 ...", and step 2.1 says, "The standard local-to-global boundary argument for C^2 domains, exactly as in the harvested Boas proof of Theorem 10, upgrades these local models to global Hartogs pseudoconvexity." None of the opened dependencies (`def-plurisubharmonic-exhaustion-and-hartogs-pseudoconvexity`, `def-levi-pseudoconvex-domain`, `lem-levi-pseudoconvexity-is-independent-of-defining-function`, `thm-c-two-levi-criterion-for-plurisubharmonicity`) contains either imported argument. The converse direction is therefore not proved from current disk.
